label: Fig1.
title: Default workflows diverge in filtering and HVGs
note:
Figure 1. Default workflows diverge in filtering and HVGs

Figure 1. Seurat and Scanpy show considerable differences in scRNA-seq workflow results with default function arguments. (A) Filtering and HVG selection analysis UpSet plots consisting of sets of (Ai) cells, (Aii) genes, and (Aiii) HVGs. (B) (Bi) PCA through projection onto the first two PCs. (E) DE analysis UpSet plot through overlap of all significant (p < 0.05) marker genes across all clusters. Dataset used: 10,000 PBMC.

label: Fig4.
title: Cell-type, DE and pathway results diverge downstream
note:
Figure 4. Cell-type, DE and pathway results diverge downstream

Figure 4. Additional analysis underscores observed differences between Seurat and Scanpy in biologically motivated downstream analysis. (A) Alluvial plot showing cell-type mapping between Seurat and Scanpy default pipelines. (B) Volcano plot for differentially expressed genes identified by Seurat in cluster 15. (C) Volcano plot for differentially expressed genes identified by Scanpy in cluster 15. Biological significance thresholds used (dashed lines): |log FC| = 1 (vertical) and p = 0.05 (horizontal). (D) UpSet plots of the set comparison for the biologically significant (i.e., red and blue) genes selected from the volcano plots generated by Seurat and Scanpy in cluster 15. (E) GO analysis scatterplot from the Enrichr "pathway" database, given the biologically significant genes identified by Seurat and Scanpy in cluster 15. Dataset: 10,000 PBMC.

Source: Rich et al., Cell Systems 2026, combined paper + supplement PDF.
